- [2023/03/15] There are around 30 active volcanoes in Iceland.
- [2023/03/15] Some of the most dangerous active volcanoes in Iceland include Katla, Hekla, Grímsvötn, Öræfajökull, Bárðarbunga, Askja, and Eyjafjallajökull.
- [2023/03/15] The 2010 eruption of Eyjafjallajökull disrupted air traffic in Europe due to significant ash clouds.
- [2023/03/15] The 2011 eruption of Grímsvötn caused extensive flooding and disruption to air travel.
- [2023/03/15] The 2014 eruption of Bárðarbunga created a 50-square-kilometer lava field and released sulfur dioxide and other gases, impacting air quality and contributing to acid rain.
- [2023/03/15] The 1783 Laki eruption lasted eight months, releasing ash and gases that killed over 50% of Iceland's livestock and 25% of its human population due to famine and disease.
- [2023/03/15] Iceland uses GPS sensors to detect ground elevation changes caused by magma movement and has developed sophisticated computer models to predict volcanic activity.
- [2023/03/15] Iceland has an effective disaster response system with regular drills, well-equipped emergency response teams, and a comprehensive evacuation plan.
- [2023/03/15] Iceland's volcanic management strategies are studied by other countries with active volcanoes, and Iceland provides training and equipment to countries like Indonesia for monitoring volcanic activity.
